The answer to all of this lives in Execution Context. Once I understood how JavaScript prepares code before running it, hoisting stopped being confusing and started making sense. Let's break it down. Hoisting happens in the creation phase, not during the execution. Hoisting is JavaScript’s behavior of moving declarations to the top of their scope during the creation phase. Not physically moving code — but allocating memory before execution starts.
At first glance, this code looks wrong. We are calling printMessage() before defining it. We are logging x before assigning it. We are even logging the function itself. Yet… this code works. Now let's start with var.

JavaScript allocates memory Stores the entire function definition So in memory:
JavaScript already knows what printMessage() is before execution begins. This is why function declarations are fully hoisted. Now JavaScript starts executing the code from top to bottom. Line 1

entry.title: The 'Lorebook' Phenomenon: How Role-Players and Interactive Fiction Fans Are Building Complex, Persistent AI Characters
entry.summary: The Anatomy of a Master-Crafted Character Sheet This isn't a description for a reader; it's a set of instructions for an actor (the AI). It provides actionable triggers for consistent behavior. A Contrarian Take: The Lorebook Isn't for the AI. It's for the Human. The lorebook creators are the early explorers of persistent identity engineering. They are proving that AI doesn't have to be a one-session wonder; it can be the keeper of a long, evolving story. The goal isn't to build a perfect system overnight. It's to shift your mindset from seeing the AI as a single-session tool to viewing it as the steward of an ongoing narrative that you author, both in the document and in the dialogue. The most compelling stories aren't written in one sitting. They are lived, remembered, and built upon. The lorebook phenomenon shows us that with a little old-fashioned note-taking and a lot of ingenuity, our AI partners can finally remember them with us. If you were to build a lorebook for an AI to role-play your favorite fictional character or historical figure, what's the one piece of "secret lore" or psychological detail you'd include that most people wouldn't know, but that would make the character truly come alive?
